name: @dudo/client-kdf
description: Client-side credential derivation — ADR 0015 §D. One implementation, both browser consoles, and the shared test vectors Dudo-Apple must reproduce.
//: WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE PACKAGE FROM @dudo/ui, AND IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF
OF ADR 0040.
One shared package would have been simpler and would have quietly destroyed
0036's no-authority rule. Put `kdf.ts` beside `button.tsx` and 'the shared
package' becomes a place where presentation and CREDENTIAL DERIVATION both
live — at which point the next author importing something that decides from it
has broken no visible rule. The split is what keeps that sentence enforceable,
and it is what gives `check:ui-purity` a subject it can actually cover.
THIS PACKAGE IS THE OPPOSITE KIND OF THING AND IS TREATED ACCORDINGLY: it is
security-relevant, it carries no components and no styling, and its output is a
43-character credential that Core will accept or refuse.
IT HAS NO DEPENDENCIES AT ALL. The derivation runs on the platform's own
WebCrypto — `crypto.subtle.deriveBits` with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 — and normalises
with `String.prototype.normalize`. Nothing is installed, and nothing should be:
a supply-chain surface on the login path is the one place it costs most.
THE SUITE SHIPS WITH THE CODE. `scripts/verify-kdf.mjs` imports the REAL module
rather than a copy, so it checks what the browsers ship. It is the UNION of the
two suites the consoles used to carry separately — 17 assertions were present in
one and absent from the other, including the printable-ASCII boundary on the
login path — and `check:suite-parity` reached 0 before this package existed,
which is what proved the union complete rather than convenient.
